# docker_swarm_node

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: resource. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Joins a Docker host to an existing swarm. The join is sent to the joining node's OWN daemon (`host`, optionally with a `tls` block); availability, role and labels are then set through the provider's Docker host, which must be a swarm manager. Destroying the resource makes the node leave the swarm (force), waits until the manager reports it down, and removes it from the node list (managers are demoted first).

Import with the node ID; `host`, `join_token` and `manager_address` must then be set in configuration (the next apply records them without replacing the node).

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `advertise_addr` | `string` | optional | yes |  | Address the node advertises, `<ip\|interface>[:port]`. Changing this forces a new resource. |
| `availability` | `string` | optional, computed |  |  | Scheduling availability: `active`, `pause` or `drain`. Default `active`. Updated in place through the manager. |
| `host` | `string` | required | yes |  | Docker endpoint of the JOINING node, e.g. `tcp://10.0.0.6:2376`. Changing this forces a new resource. |
| `hostname` | `string` | computed |  |  | Hostname the node reports to the swarm. |
| `id` | `string` | computed |  |  | Swarm node ID (same as `node_id`). |
| `join_token` | `string` | required | yes | yes | Worker or manager join token, e.g. `docker_swarm_init.this.worker_join_token`. Changing this forces a new resource. |
| `labels` | `map(string)` | optional |  |  | Node labels (`node.labels.*` in placement constraints). Updated in place; labels set outside Terraform are removed. |
| `listen_addr` | `string` | optional, computed | yes |  | Listen address for swarm traffic on the node. Default `0.0.0.0:2377`. Changing this forces a new resource. |
| `manager_address` | `string` | required | yes |  | Address of an existing manager as seen from the joining node, e.g. `10.0.0.5:2377`. Changing this forces a new resource. |
| `node_id` | `string` | computed |  |  | Swarm node ID, read from the joining daemon after the join. |
| `role` | `string` | optional, computed |  |  | Node role: `worker` or `manager`. Default `worker`. Updated in place (promote/demote) through the manager, whichever token was used to join. |

Nested blocks: `tls` (single block).

### `tls`

single block. TLS client material for the joining node's `tcp://` `host`. Each value is PEM content or a path to a PEM file. Only used to reach that daemon; changing it does not replace the node.

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ca` | `string` | optional |  |  | CA certificate (PEM or path). |
| `cert` | `string` | optional |  |  | Client certificate (PEM or path). |
| `key` | `string` | optional |  | yes | Client private key (PEM or path). |

## Example

```terraform
# The provider points at a swarm manager; each docker_swarm_node reaches the
# joining machine through its own Docker endpoint.
resource "docker_swarm_init" "this" {
  advertise_addr = "10.0.0.5"
}

resource "docker_swarm_node" "worker1" {
  host            = "tcp://10.0.0.6:2376"
  join_token      = docker_swarm_init.this.worker_join_token
  manager_address = "10.0.0.5:2377"
  advertise_addr  = "10.0.0.6"

  tls {
    ca   = "~/.docker/worker1/ca.pem"
    cert = "~/.docker/worker1/cert.pem"
    key  = "~/.docker/worker1/key.pem"
  }

  availability = "active"
  role         = "worker"
  labels = {
    zone = "a"
  }
}
```

## Import

```shell
# The import ID is the swarm node ID. After importing, host, join_token and
# manager_address must be set in configuration; the next apply records them
# without replacing the node.
terraform import docker_swarm_node.worker1 r6ys9kxnbyl0q7n4w9l7ynqfr
```
